title: You Should Totally Buy a Business Instead of Job Hunting
content: There are two major types of people who should buy businesses to run them and operate them like a really good job and that's okay. I'm Sarah Sharpen, the deal attorney at help people buy themselves. Businesses every day, specifically accounting practices and a lot of the people that I work with are folks who are buying a business as an investment tool and they're going to resell it later for more under a different like a variety of different circumstances, right? Whether they're combining companies to sell a greater multiple or they're buying one that's bigly profitable and they're planning on you know turning it around or increasing the profits so that they can sell it for more. But usually the five-distance plan your plan for folks like that is to sell to a bigger you know fish in the ocean. That is not everyone I work with though. A lot of folks that I work with are buying a business to run a business and sometimes people are say like oh you're just buying a nice job which is they say like a negative thing but having a good job is a great thing. So the people who really ought to buy businesses to run them and just have a great life-life I'll business especially accounting practices are in my opinion number one folks to are relocating. So I've had so many people who have always wanted to live somewhere particular in the world and they wanted to move closer to family something like that and it's a small town type of thing. So they're looking for a job and there's not a lot of jobs out there specifically not a lot of high-paying jobs. So when you're moving from the city whatever city that is to small town America it can be hard to match your lifestyle by you're getting some kind of entry-level job. Great solution for accountants doing that is to buy the main street accounting firm next door and it comes with a kind of not just a job and an office and employees. It also comes with like a place in the culture of the community which you can't really put a price tag on. So I think that's such a nice fit and I love helping people with relocation acquisition whether they're moving to small town America or they're moving just to another city where they wanted to live. I've helped people who you know are moving to a city that they always travel to for fly fishing or golfing or whatever and they're just making their dreams come true and it's really fun. That's a phenomenal way to relocate the second big group of people who should buy a business to run the business like an awesome job are people who are not newbies. So if you've got any expenses you don't have to you could absolutely start your own thing and a lot of folks do they'll start you know firm you could move to wherever and start your own firm but you're going to wind up with like if you already have a mortgage you already have some you know kids you've got a lifestyle that's built around what you can make you're probably going to find yourself in a sticky situation starting from scratch it's going to be you know the slow growth is not really worth it. So if you have you know built your life on making a hundred and twenty thousand dollars and you've got forty thousand dollars of people you can you know provide services to in your one you're going to have you know a pretty big delta between your living expenses and what you're able to make so it makes a lot of sense then instead of taking out a big loan to bridge the gap on those living expenses while you get up to speed you instead take out a loan by a firm that you know will spit off at least enough profit to belt to live the way that you're accustomed to and pay on that loan because at the end of that loan term you will also have leveraged your way up so you won't have started from scratch and had five to ten years experience you'll have started from you know essentially a twenty year experience and be building up so you know those I think make a lot of sense I very rarely have folks write out a college trying to buy a firm for the purposes of operating it because those folks might be best suited by you know just starting from scratch and they don't have any experience so it's hard to convince sellers to sell to them but I do oh big bird I do think that a lot of folks who have already built a life and are trying to make the move it makes more sense to get you know usually an SBA seven a loan buy a firm that has enough profit margin for you to build a mature salary or whatever you need to live on and then grow it slowly and carefully while you're paying off the loan so those are the two people who can run their businesses as owner operators and not feel guilty about it if this was valuable at all please swipe up and comment and like and subscribe
description:
Buying a business doesn’t always mean becoming the next private equity mogul, and that’s okay.

If you’ve ever been told that buying a business “just to run it” is settling for a glorified job… this one’s for you.

In this video, I share the two types of people who are perfect candidates to buy an accounting practice and operate it like a lifestyle business, without shame, and with plenty of ROI.

Whether you're relocating to small-town America and looking for a way to maintain your lifestyle income, or you’re a mid-career professional who can’t afford to spend three years building from scratch, buying the right firm might be the smartest move you make.

You’ll learn:
✔️ Why relocation buyers are uniquely positioned to succeed
✔️ How buying a firm can replace your income immediately
✔️ The math behind SBA loans vs. bootstrapping
✔️ Who shouldn’t try to buy and operate a firm solo

This is real talk for real people who want a stable business, not just a unicorn exit.

For more information on Deal Academy, a program that teaches you how to buy and sell accounting practices, click the link here:
https://www.dealacademy.org

To connect with Sara Sharp on LinkedIn:
https://www.linkedin.com/in/sara-sharp-9a2a98b/

For more information on our Mergers and Acquisitions law practice click here:
https://www.skandslegal.com
